title: What Does Marketing Do?
subtitle: Simple words for what a marketing team does every day
description: Learn the basic words for marketing activities and how to say simply what your team does.
dialogueSubtitle: Riley explains to Dana what the Brightline marketing team does every day

vocabulary.definition: To tell people about a product or brand and help them like it.
vocabulary.example: We promote our products on social media and at events.

vocabulary.definition: To pay to show information about a product to many people.
vocabulary.example: We advertise on Google and social media to reach more people.

vocabulary.definition: To give something to someone for money.
vocabulary.example: Our goal is to help the sales team sell more products this month.

vocabulary.definition: To start something new — like a product or campaign — for the first time.
vocabulary.example: We will launch the new product in March.

vocabulary.definition: To share information with other people.
vocabulary.example: Marketing helps the company communicate with its clients and the public.

vocabulary.definition: To send or show something to other people.
vocabulary.example: We share news about the brand on social media every week.

vocabulary.definition: To get to or connect with a group of people.
vocabulary.example: Our last campaign reached 10,000 people online.
We create content for our website and social media every week.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Tell many people about something — a product, event, or brand.
phrasalVerbs.example: Our job is to get the word out about the new product before it launches.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Contact a person or group of people to talk or share information.
phrasalVerbs.example: We reach out to clients by email to tell them about new products.
The team came up with a great idea for the next campaign.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Make or organise something, like a plan or a piece of content.
phrasalVerbs.example: Riley put together a short video to promote the new product.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Start to use or share something with a lot of people.
phrasalVerbs.example: We will roll out the new campaign next week.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Contact someone again after a first conversation or message.
phrasalVerbs.example: After the event, we follow up with new contacts by email.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Riley, can you tell me — what does the marketing team actually do every day?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Sure! Our main job is to [[promote:to tell people about a product or brand and help them like it]] Brightline — to help people know who we are and what we do.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: We [[create:to make something new]] content every week — things like blog posts, videos, and social media posts. We also [[advertise:to pay to show information about a product to many people]] on Google and social media.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: How many people do you try to [[reach:to get to or connect with a group of people]]?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Our last campaign reached about 50,000 people online. We try to reach more people every month.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Do you also help to [[sell:to give something to someone for money]] the product?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes — we work closely with the sales team. Our job is to bring people in and help them understand the product. The sales team then does the selling.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: And when you [[launch:to start something new for the first time]] a new product — what does marketing do?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: We plan everything ahead of time — the content, the ads, the emails. We want to [[communicate:to share information with other people]] the news clearly to all our clients.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Do you [[share:to send or show something to other people]] the news on social media too?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes — social media is a big part of how we launch. We share posts, short videos, and sometimes do a live event online.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: It sounds like the marketing team does a lot. I had no idea how much work goes into it.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the question. Talk about which answer (A, B, or C) is best. Choose together, then click to check.

items.customerLine: What does your marketing team actually do?
options: We do a lot of different things.
We promote the brand, create content, advertise on Google and social media, and help launch new products.
We work with the sales team.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives four clear examples of what the team does. A is too vague. C only says one thing and it is about another team, not marketing.

items.customerLine: How do you reach new clients?
options: We advertise on Google and social media, and we create content that helps people find us online. We also reach out by email after events.
We have a good system for that.
items.explanation: B is correct. It names real channels — Google, social media, email — and says how each one works. A gives no information. C sounds good but says nothing useful.

items.customerLine: Are you launching any new products soon?
options: Yes — we are launching a new plan in March. We are already creating content and planning the ads.
Yes, we have a launch coming up.
We always have new things in the pipeline.
items.explanation: A is correct. It says when the launch is and what the team is already doing to prepare. B is too short and gives no detail. C sounds vague and does not really answer the question.

items.customerLine: How does marketing help the sales team?
options: Marketing brings people in and helps them understand the product. Then the sales team takes over and does the selling.
items.explanation: B is correct. It explains the two steps clearly — marketing brings people in, sales closes the deal. A and C say very little and do not explain how marketing actually helps.

profileMatch.instructions: You are Riley. Three people ask about what marketing does. As a group, talk about which way to explain it fits each situation best. Click 'Check Matches' when you agree.

profiles.name: A new team member from another department
profiles.description: A new person from the finance team asks what marketing does. They have never worked near a marketing team before.

profiles.name: A client asking before they sign a contract
profiles.description: A client wants to know how Brightline's marketing team will promote their brand if they become a client.

profiles.name: A contact at a networking event
profiles.description: Someone at an event asks what marketing does. They work in a different industry. You have about 30 seconds.

options.label: Clear and simple
options.description: Explain the basics — promote, advertise, create content, communicate. Use simple words and give one or two examples. Best for someone who does not know much about marketing.

options.label: What we do for you
options.description: Explain what the marketing team will do for the client specifically — which channels, what kind of content, and how they will communicate. Best when the person needs to know exactly what they are buying.

options.label: One clear sentence
options.description: Say what marketing does in one sentence — for example, 'We help companies tell people about their products.' Best when you do not have much time.

finishTheLine.instructions: The marketer's line is not finished. As a group, talk about how you would finish it. Use words from this lesson. There is no one right answer — share your ideas, then click to see one example.
